text:
There was a campsite we liked. Right on the beach. You wake up in the morning and jump straight into the sea.

But then the Israel Nature and Parks Authority prohibited staying overnight at the site. You can still visit the beach, but not sleep.

Of course, we were disappointed. Until I learned more.

Turns out sea turtles nest on that beach, and people get in their way. Light and noise. Females come ashore at night to lay their eggs, and if someone disturbs them, they go back to the sea without nesting. About two months later, the hatchlings dig out at night and crawl toward the brightest horizon, which is normally the sea. A campfire or a flashlight can lead them inland instead.

That is likely one of the reasons the campsite was closed.

Spent half a day learning about cases like that with my kids at the Museum of Natural History at Tel Aviv University. Lots of interactive exhibits we could play with to learn how humans and nature interact and how we can do better. Talked a lot about it all the way home.
